senses.gloss: to divine, to make action dependent on an omen, to augur.
units: <cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 7:8">Tosef. Sabb. VII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 8:13">VIII</cite>), 13 <he>איזהו מְנַחֵשׁ וכ׳</he> a diviner (under the law, <cite ref="Leviticus 19:26">Lev. XIX, 26</cite>) is he who says, ‘my staff fell out of my hand’ (it portends evil) &c.; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 65b:20">Snh. 65ᵇ</cite>.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 66a:2">Ib. 66ᵃ</cite> <he>כגון אלו המְנַחֲשִׁים בחולדה וכ׳</he> like those who divine (evil or luck) from a weasel, birds &c. Y. Sabb. VI, end, 8ᵈ <he>כל המנחש סופו לבוא עליו</he> if one believes in omens, what he fears will finally befall him (with ref. to <he>לא נחש</he> <cite ref="Numbers 23:23">Num. XXIII, 23</cite>, changed into <he>לו נחש</he>); <cite ref="Nedarim 32a:13">Ned. 32ᵃ</cite> <he>כל המנחש לו נחש</he> for him who believes in omens, the omen exists (will be realized).

<cite ref="Nedarim 32a:13">Ib.</cite> <he>כל אדם שאינו מנ׳</he> he who rejects divination. Mekh. B’shall. s. 2 <he>שמא יְנַחֲשׁוּ ויחזרו וכ׳</he> lest they consider it a bad omen and go back. Ib. <he>וזקני מדין נִחֲשׁוּ וכ׳</he> and the Midianite elders considered (Balaam’s death) a bad omen and went home; a. fr.—Sifra Vayikra, Par. 9, ch. XIII (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 18:3">Lev. XVIII, 3</cite>) [read:] <he>שלא תְנַחֵשׁ</he> thou must not augur (v. however, <cite ref="N01243"><he>נָקַר</he> II</cite>).
